nodes.title: Weighted measures
nodes.statement: Define AbstractMeasure.weight g : D(X,R) →ₗ[R] D(X,R) by (weight g μ)(f)=μ(gf). This acts on the existing carrier, not a second definition of bounded measures.
hypotheses: X is a compact topological space; R is a normed commutative ring; g : C(X,R), μ : D(X,R). No topology is newly imposed on AbstractMeasure.
proofSteps: Continuous functions on compact X form a normed commutative ring. Promote LinearMap.mulLeft R g to a continuous linear map by continuity of multiplication (also ‖gf‖≤‖g‖‖f‖). No scalar field is required.
Use AbstractMeasure.toCLMEquiv to transport μ, precompose with multiplication by g and transport back. Linearity in μ is inherited from composition.
The defining evaluation law gives weight 1=id, weight 0=0, constant-scalar compatibility and the Dirac formula. Weighting by x need not be invertible: it kills δ₀.

nodes.title: Composition of weights
nodes.statement: For g,h : C(X,R), weight (gh) μ=weight g (weight h μ).
hypotheses: X is a compact topological space; R is a normed commutative ring; g : C(X,R), μ : D(X,R). No topology is newly imposed on AbstractMeasure.
proofSteps: Use measure extensionality and weight-evaluation twice. The right side at f is μ(h(gf)); associativity and commutativity identify it with μ((gh)f).

nodes.title: Projection formula for weights
nodes.statement: For compact Y, h : C(X,Y), g : C(Y,R), AbstractMeasure.map h (weight (g.comp h) μ)=weight g (AbstractMeasure.map h μ).
hypotheses: X is a compact topological space; R is a normed commutative ring; g : C(X,R), μ : D(X,R). No topology is newly imposed on AbstractMeasure.
proofSteps: Evaluate at f : C(Y,R). The existing map_apply and weight-evaluation reduce both sides to μ((g∘h)(f∘h)). No new pushforward is defined.

nodes.title: Iterated weighting
nodes.statement: For k∈ℕ and f : C(X,R), ((weight g)^[k] μ)(f)=μ(g^k f).
hypotheses: X is a compact topological space; R is a normed commutative ring; g : C(X,R), μ : D(X,R). No topology is newly imposed on AbstractMeasure.
proofSteps: Induct on k. At zero, μ(f)=μ(1f). At the successor step apply weight-evaluation and the induction hypothesis at gf, then use g^k(gf)=g^(k+1)f. Weight-multiplication records the same action identity.

nodes.title: Mahler derivation
nodes.statement: Define PowerSeries.mahlerDerivation R : Derivation R R⟦T⟧ R⟦T⟧ as (1+T) • PowerSeries.derivative R. Write ∂F=(1+T)DF.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; F : R⟦T⟧. D is the existing formal derivative; ∂ is mahlerDerivation R.
proofSteps: Reuse the existing Derivation scalar action and formal derivative. Multiplying the derivation by 1+T inherits linearity, vanishing on constants and Leibniz.
Unfold scalar action for the explicit apply law. This operator never divides by F and is different from Coleman's logarithmic derivative.

acceptance: Valid over every commutative ring, including positive characteristic. Its kernel is not claimed to consist only of constants.

nodes.title: Pseudomeasures
nodes.statement: Define Iwasawa.pseudomeasures δ Q : Submodule R Q to be (1 : Submodule R Q) / Submodule.span R (range (g ↦ ι(δ(g)−1))). This uses the existing submodule quotient. It is an R-module; it is not asserted to be a subring, a fractional ideal in the domain-specific sense, or a topological completion.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
proofSteps: Use the existing total quotient ring and Submodule.div. The unit submodule is the image of R by Submodule.one_eq_range.
Take the span of the Dirac differences and the quotient of the unit submodule by that span. All additive and R-module structure is inherited.
Subtype extensionality is routine. If δ(g)=1 for every g, the span is zero and the defining membership condition holds for every q ∈ Q.

nodes.title: Evaluation equation
nodes.statement: For an admissible g and every pseudomeasure z, f(c_g) evalAt_g(z)=f(n_g(z)).
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)).
proofSteps: Unfold evaluation and cancel the unit with its chosen inverse.
acceptance: For R=ℤ, Q=A=ℚ, δ=Units.coeHom ℤ, g=−1 and z=1/2, the equation is (−2)(1/2)=−1.

nodes.title: Independence of clearing factor
nodes.statement: If f(c_g) and f(c_h) are units, evalAt δ Q A g hg = evalAt δ Q A h hh as R-linear maps.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)); hh : IsUnit (f(c_h)).
proofSteps: Apply f to cross-multiplied-numerators.
Substitute the two evaluation equations. Commutativity gives f(c_h)f(c_g)evalAt_g(z)=f(c_h)f(c_g)evalAt_h(z).
Cancel the two units with IsUnit.mul_left_cancel. Extensionality of linear maps gives the result. This also removes any dependence on the witness of IsUnit.
acceptance: With g=h the result identifies any two witnesses of the same IsUnit condition. With distinct g,h the proof must use the cross-numerator relation and cancellation of units, and must not assume a ring homomorphism from Q to A.

nodes.title: Evaluation of integral measures
nodes.statement: For every r ∈ R and admissible g, evalAt_g(integral r)=f(r).
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)).
proofSteps: Map the numerator specification for integral r to Q and use integral-inclusion-value; injectivity identifies the numerator with c_g r.
Use the evaluation equation and cancel f(c_g) with IsUnit.mul_left_cancel.
acceptance: For R=ℤ, Q=A=ℚ, δ=Units.coeHom ℤ and g=−1, evaluation of integral 3 is 3. The result also holds for r=0 and r=1.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of admissible evaluation
nodes.statement: Let g be admissible. If L : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] A satisfies L(integral r)=f(r) for every r, then L=evalAt_g.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)); L is R-linear and extends f on the integral inclusion.
proofSteps: For each z, prove c_g • z = integral(n_g(z)) by subtype extensionality, integral-inclusion-value and cleared-numerator-spec.
Apply L and use R-linearity and the extension condition to obtain f(c_g)L(z)=f(n_g(z)).
Compare with admissible-evaluation-spec and cancel the unit.
acceptance: For R=ℤ, Q=A=ℚ and δ=Units.coeHom ℤ, every ℤ-linear extension of integer inclusion must send 1/2 to 1/2, since doubling that element gives integral 1. No multiplicative structure on the pseudomeasure carrier is assumed.

nodes.title: Evaluation under coefficient change
nodes.statement: Let k : A →ₐ[R] B with B a commutative R-algebra. For g admissible in A and in B, k(evalAt_g^A(z))=evalAt_g^B(z). The second admissibility follows automatically from IsUnit.map and the algebra-map compatibility of k.
hypotheses: G is a group; R is a commutative ring; δ : G →* R is given. No topological hypotheses are needed for this algebraic subproblem.
Q is a commutative R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q. The canonical map ι : R → Q is injective; Q means the total quotient ring, not an assumed field.
A is a commutative R-algebra. Write f = algebraMap R A and c_g = δ(g)−1.
B is a commutative R-algebra; k : A →ₐ[R] B; g has unit factor in A (hence also in B).
proofSteps: Map the evaluation equation from A to B using k.
The R-algebra law identifies k(f_A(c_g)) with f_B(c_g), and likewise for n_g(z).
Compare with the evaluation equation in B and cancel its unit. Identity and composition compatibility follow by specializing k and evaluating composed functions.
acceptance: For k=id_A the equality is reflexive; applying it successively along A→B→C gives the same equality as the composite. In particular it transports the rational value 1/2 along ℚ→ℝ in the integer-units example.

nodes.title: Obstruction to total quotient evaluation
nodes.statement: Let f : R →+* A with A a nontrivial commutative ring. If s ∈ nonZeroDivisors R and f(s)=0, there is no F : Q →+* A with F.comp (algebraMap R Q)=f.
hypotheses: R,Q are commutative rings, Q is an R-algebra with IsFractionRing R Q.
A is a nontrivial commutative ring; f : R →+* A; s is a non-zero-divisor of R killed by f.
proofSteps: IsLocalization.map_units makes ι(s) a unit in Q.
If F existed, IsUnit.map would make F(ι(s))=f(s)=0 a unit in A, contradicting not_isUnit_zero.
The existing IsLocalization.lift has the stronger denominator hypothesis needed to extend a map on all of Q. It supplies no such lift merely because f is a character integral.
acceptance: For R=ℚ[X], evaluation at 0 kills the regular element X, so it cannot extend to FractionRing R.
For R=ℚ[X], evaluation at 3 kills the regular element X−3; nonzero evaluation points do not resolve the obstruction.
The condition that 2 ≠ 0 in ℤ does not make 2 invertible; general-target evaluation must require IsUnit.

nodes.title: The clopen subset pZ_p
nodes.statement: U=pZ is clopen in Z.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, U={x∈Z : p divides x}=pZ. R is a normed commutative ring and D(Z,R) is the existing AbstractMeasure continuous dual. χ is the existing LocallyConstant.charFn of U, coerced to C(Z,R); m_p(x)=px. No topology is imposed on D(Z,R).
proofSteps: By norm_lt_one_iff_dvd, U is the inverse image of the open interval (−∞,1) under the norm, hence open.
U is the image of compact Z under the continuous map m_p. This image is compact and hence closed in the metric space Z. Equality with the divisibility set is the definition of divisibility.
acceptance: For p=2, zero and 2 lie in U and 1 does not.

nodes.title: Exact division on pZ_p
nodes.statement: Define divideByP : C(Z,Z) by q(px)=x and q(y)=0 for y outside U.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, U={x∈Z : p divides x}=pZ. R is a normed commutative ring and D(Z,R) is the existing AbstractMeasure continuous dual. χ is the existing LocallyConstant.charFn of U, coerced to C(Z,R); m_p(x)=px. No topology is imposed on D(Z,R).
proofSteps: Multiplication by the nonzero scalar p in the characteristic-zero domain Z gives a continuous bijection Z→U. Surjectivity is divisibility; injectivity is cancellation. Bundle its ordinary inverse as an equivalence.
Use Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2 to make this equivalence a homeomorphism. Its inverse is continuous on the subspace U.

Extend the inverse by zero off U. On the closed set U it is continuous by the subtype criterion, and on the closed complement it is constant. The frontier is empty, so continuous_piecewise pastes these maps without a boundary condition. Bundle the resulting continuous function.
acceptance: The extension convention is zero off U, not an inverse for the ring operation p in Z.

nodes.statement: Define psiMeasure=(AbstractMeasure.map q)∘restrictMultiples as an R-linear endomorphism of D(Z,R). Denote it ψ.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, U={x∈Z : p divides x}=pZ. R is a normed commutative ring and D(Z,R) is the existing AbstractMeasure continuous dual. χ is the existing LocallyConstant.charFn of U, coerced to C(Z,R); m_p(x)=px. No topology is imposed on D(Z,R).

hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, U={x∈Z : p divides x}=pZ. R is a normed commutative ring and D(Z,R) is the existing AbstractMeasure continuous dual. χ is the existing LocallyConstant.charFn of U, coerced to C(Z,R); m_p(x)=px. No topology is imposed on D(Z,R).

nodes.title: Mahler expansion under dilation
nodes.statement: For n≥0 and x∈Z, mahler_n(px)=Σ_(0≤k≤n) coeff_n(b^k) mahler_k(x).
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z⟦T⟧, b=(1+T)^p−1. A is the pinned integral Z-linear Amice equivalence. Formal substitution at b has zero constant term; no analytic evaluation or field-coefficient inverse is asserted.
proofSteps: At x=m a natural number, expand (1+T)^(pm)=(1+b)^m by add_pow. Coefficients of (1+T)^(pm) are binomial(pm,n), using Polynomial.coeff_one_add_X_pow and Polynomial.coeff_coe. The right side has coefficient Σ_k binomial(m,k) coeff_n(b^k).

Since constantCoeff b=0, le_order_pow_of_constantCoeff_eq_zero and coeff_of_lt_order give coeff_n(b^k)=0 for k>n. Terms k>m also vanish by the natural binomial convention. Thus both finite ranges can be replaced by 0≤k≤n. mahler_natCast_eq identifies the claimed natural-point identity.

Both sides are continuous functions of x: the left is a continuous Mahler function composed with multiplication by p; the right is a finite linear combination of continuous Mahler functions. Apply denseRange_natCast and DenseRange.equalizer to extend to all Z.
acceptance: At p=3,n=2: binomial(3x,2)=3 binomial(x,1)+9 binomial(x,2), checked by the suggested example.

nodes.title: Identification of p-adic unit inverses
nodes.statement: For every z∈Z, PadicInt.inv z=Ring.inverse z. Both functions already exist; no new inverse function is defined.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p with its pinned norm topology. D=D(Z,Z) is the existing integral AbstractMeasure carrier, x is the identity continuous function, and W=weight x. Write r=unitRestriction p Z and ψ=psiMeasure p Z. No topology on the measure carrier is newly imposed.
proofSteps: For a unit z, PadicInt.mul_inv and isUnit_iff give z·PadicInt.inv(z)=1. Ring.mul_inverse_cancel gives z·Ring.inverse(z)=1. Cancel the nonzero z.
For a nonunit z, isUnit_iff implies ‖z‖≠1. Unfold the existing PadicInt.inv conditional using norm_eq_padic_norm: its value is zero. Ring.inverse_non_unit gives the same value.

nodes.title: Continuity of the extended unit inverse
nodes.statement: The existing function PadicInt.inv:Z→Z is continuous, including at zero and at every nonunit.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p with its pinned norm topology. D=D(Z,Z) is the existing integral AbstractMeasure carrier, x is the identity continuous function, and W=weight x. Write r=unitRestriction p Z and ψ=psiMeasure p Z. No topology on the measure carrier is newly imposed.
proofSteps: Replace the existing function by Ring.inverse using padic-unit-inverse-identification.
At a unit u, apply NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt. The p-adic integer ring is a complete normed ring and supplies HasSummableGeomSeries; it is not treated as a field.

At a nonunit z, PadicInt.not_isUnit_iff gives ‖z‖<1. The open set {w:‖w‖<1} is a neighbourhood of z. Ring.inverse is identically zero there by inverse_non_unit. Transfer continuity from the constant-zero function via eventual equality.

hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p with its pinned norm topology. D=D(Z,Z) is the existing integral AbstractMeasure carrier, x is the identity continuous function, and W=weight x. Write r=unitRestriction p Z and ψ=psiMeasure p Z. No topology on the measure carrier is newly imposed.
proofSteps: The inverse identification and Ring.inverse_mul applied to the unit a give ι(a z)=a⁻¹ι(z) for every z, including nonunits; Ring.inverse_unit fixes the inverse convention.
At f the left side is μ((ιf)∘d_a)=μ((ι∘d_a)(f∘d_a)). Substitute the pointwise identity, pull out the scalar a⁻¹ using measure linearity, and use inverseWeight_apply and map_apply for the right side.

nodes.title: The linear topology on the receiving integer ring
nodes.statement: The induced topology on O=Valued.integer(ℂ_p) is a linear ring topology: zero has a basis of open ideals.
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

C_p is the pinned PadicComplex field, O is its existing valuation integer ring with the induced topology, and j₀:Z→C_p is the composite through ℚ_p. Power series carry the coefficientwise p-adic topology, not the uniform coefficient norm topology. Write j:Z→O for integral-coefficient-map and τ_i for root-translation whenever they occur.
proofSteps: Use the existing valuation integer ring, not a new ring or a discrete topology. Its norm is the induced p-adic norm and its elements have norm at most 1.

For each positive radius r≤1, the elements of O with norm less than r form an ideal: the ultrametric inequality proves additivity and multiplication by an element of O cannot increase the norm. These are exactly the valuation ltIdeal balls.

The induced valued-field neighborhood basis is this ideal basis. Apply IsLinearTopology.mk_of_hasBasis. Completeness is supplied separately by the pinned closed-integer-subspace theorem; no finiteness or discretely valued hypothesis is imposed on O.

nodes.title: Prime roots of unity are close to one
nodes.statement: For every ζ∈ℂ_p with ζ^p=1, including ζ=1 and p=2, one has |ζ−1|<1.
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

C_p is the pinned PadicComplex field, O is its existing valuation integer ring with the induced topology, and j₀:Z→C_p is the composite through ℚ_p. Power series carry the coefficientwise p-adic topology, not the uniform coefficient norm topology. Write j:Z→O for integral-coefficient-map and τ_i for root-translation whenever they occur.
proofSteps: Since p>0 and ζ^p=1, ζ has finite order and the pinned finite-order norm lemma gives |ζ|=1. Thus w=ζ−1 satisfies |w|≤1 by ultrametricity.
Expand (1+w)^p=1. For 1≤k<p, the integer binomial coefficient binom(p,k) is divisible by p. Thus w^p is minus the sum of binom(p,k)w^k over this range.
Every summand has norm at most |p|=1/p<1. The ultrametric inequality yields |w|^p≤1/p, hence |w|<1. No unjustified substitution or assumption on a finite extension occurs.

nodes.title: Uniform tails for integral Amice evaluation
nodes.statement: For f∈C(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) and ε>0 there is N such that, for every F∈ℤ_p[[T]] and n≥N, |invTransform(F)(f)−Σ_{k<n} c_k(f)·coeff_k(F)|<ε, where c_k(f) is its pinned Mahler coefficient.
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

C_p is the pinned PadicComplex field, O is its existing valuation integer ring with the induced topology, and j₀:Z→C_p is the composite through ℚ_p. Power series carry the coefficientwise p-adic topology, not the uniform coefficient norm topology. Write j:Z→O for integral-coefficient-map and τ_i for root-translation whenever they occur.
proofSteps: Use the exact pinned invTransform_apply series, whose Mahler coefficients c_k(f) tend to zero.
Choose N so that |c_k(f)|≤ε/2 for every k≥N. The choice is independent of F because every integral coefficient of F has norm at most 1.

Split off the finite sum. Each remaining term has norm at most ε/2. The ultrametric sum bound gives a tail norm at most ε/2, which is strictly less than ε. The smaller bound is needed to preserve strictness after taking the infinite sum. The indexed prerequisite names the multiplicative source declaration; its generated additive counterpart is IsUltrametricDist.norm_tsum_le_of_forall_le, whose exact telescope was compiled and checked.

hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

C_p is the pinned PadicComplex field, O is its existing valuation integer ring with the induced topology, and j₀:Z→C_p is the composite through ℚ_p. Power series carry the coefficientwise p-adic topology, not the uniform coefficient norm topology. Write j:Z→O for integral-coefficient-map and τ_i for root-translation whenever they occur.
proofSteps: Each finite Mahler pairing is a finite sum of continuous coefficient projections multiplied by fixed constants.
The preceding uniform tail estimate proves uniform convergence of those finite pairings to the actual inverse Amice evaluation. The uniform limit is continuous.
This is continuity against a fixed test function. It neither identifies the coefficientwise topology with the sup norm on coefficients nor asserts norm continuity of the full inverse transform.

nodes.title: Coefficientwise continuity of bounded psi
nodes.statement: The existing bounded integral operator psiSeries:ℤ_p[[T]]→ℤ_p[[T]] is continuous for the coefficientwise p-adic topology.
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

proofSteps: For a fixed coefficient n, use the actual Amice transport and psi-evaluation: coeff_n(psiSeries F)=invTransform(F)(χ·(mahler_n∘q)), where χ is the clopen pℤ_p indicator and q is the existing extended exact-division map.
The indicated test function is continuous and integral. Apply inverse-amice-evaluation-continuous.
Continuity of every coefficient proves continuity into the product topology. No ring-homomorphism property of psi is used.

nodes.title: The bounded projector on natural powers
nodes.statement: For n∈ℕ, φ(psiSeries((1+T)^n)) equals (1+T)^n if p divides n and equals zero otherwise.
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

proofSteps: Use amice-dirac-natural to write the input as the transform of δ_n.
The existing phi-psi theorem gives restriction of δ_n to pℤ_p. Its value is δ_n precisely when p divides the p-adic integer n, and is zero otherwise.
For natural n, divisibility by p in ℤ_p agrees with ordinary divisibility. Transform back using the Dirac formula.

nodes.title: Finite root orthogonality
nodes.statement: For a commutative domain R, ζ∈R primitive of order p and n∈ℕ, Σ_{i<p} ζ^(in) is p if p divides n, and zero otherwise.
hypotheses: R is a commutative domain; ζ has exact order p; n is a natural number.
proofSteps: If p divides n, ζ^n=1 and every summand is 1.
Otherwise ζ^n≠1 by the primitive-root divisibility criterion. Multiplying the geometric sum by ζ^n−1 gives (ζ^n)^p−1=0. The first factor is nonzero; cancellation in the domain gives a zero sum.
No inverse of p is introduced. The formula also holds in receiving integral rings.

nodes.title: Root averaging of polynomial transforms
nodes.statement: For ζ∈O primitive of order p and P∈ℤ_p[T], p·map(j,φ(psiSeries P))=Σ_{i<p}τ_i(P) in O[[T]].
hypotheses: p is a prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p, B=Z[[T]], Y=1+T and b=Y^p−1. A is the pinned integral Amice equivalence, φ is substitution by b, and ψ is the existing AbstractMeasure.psiSeries, with ψφ=id and φψ the pZ restriction projector.

proofSteps: First take P=(1+T)^n. The left side is p times that power exactly when p divides n, by phi-psi-natural-powers.
The right side has the same value by root-translation-natural-powers and primitive-root-power-sum.
Every polynomial P(T) is a finite ℤ_p-linear combination of powers of 1+T: expand P(U−1) in U and then put U=1+T. Both sides are ℤ_p-linear through j, so the identity extends to P.

nodes.title: Agreement on integral test functions
nodes.statement: For f in C(Z_p,Z_p), extension of mu applied to algebraMap composed with f equals algebraMap(mu(f)).
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a complete ultrametric normed commutative ring with a Z_p-algebra structure whose scalar action satisfies |a r| <= |a| |r|. No multiplicative-norm, discrete-valuation or compactness assumption on R is imposed.
proofSteps: The Mahler coefficient of algebraMap composed with f is algebraMap(a_n(f)): write this composition as f times 1_R, commute pointwise scalar multiplication through iterated forward differences, and evaluate at zero.

The inverse pairing therefore has terms algebraMap(a_n(f) coeff_n(A_mu)). The original integral pairing is summable by bounded-mahler-summable. The coefficient homomorphism is continuous by the bounded scalar action, so its map commutes with this convergent sum.
For R=Z_p, coefficient-extension-amice and the existing Amice injectivity identify the bounded inverse of these coefficients with mu. Hence the original sum is exactly mu(f).

nodes.title: Extension by zero of clopen test functions
nodes.statement: Define ContinuousMap.zeroExtendClopen s R : C(s,R) →L[R] C(X,R), denoted z_s, by z_s(f)(x)=f(x) on s and 0 off s.
hypotheses: X is a compact topological space, s is a clopen subset, and R is a normed commutative ring. No field, completeness, ultrametricity, Hausdorffness of X, or nonemptiness of s is assumed. C(s,R) uses the subspace topology and its supremum norm; s is compact because it is closed in X. D(X,R) and D(s,R) are the existing AbstractMeasure carriers. No topology is installed on either measure carrier.
proofSteps: Glue f on s and the zero function on its complement using ContinuousMap.liftCover. Both sets are open and cover X; their intersection is empty, so compatibility is vacuous. The native liftCover_coe gives the two pointwise formulas.
Addition and scalar multiplication follow pointwise on the two pieces. Compactness of s follows from IsClosed.isCompact and isCompact_iff_compactSpace.

At every point the norm of the extension is at most ‖f‖, using ContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm on s and zero off s. ContinuousMap.norm_le gives the bound ‖z_s(f)‖≤‖f‖, including s empty. Apply LinearMap.mkContinuous with constant 1. No norm-one condition on R is used.

C(s,R) uses the subspace topology and its supremum norm; s is compact because it is closed in X. D(X,R) and D(s,R) are the existing AbstractMeasure carriers. No topology is installed on either measure carrier.
proofSteps: For μ=j_sν, native map_apply evaluates every such f to ν(0)=0.
Conversely f−χ_s f vanishes on s. The annihilation assumption and linearity give μ(f)=μ(χ_s f). Apply clopen-projector-evaluation and extensionality to obtain μ=j_s r_sμ.
Uniqueness follows from clopen-restriction-section. This is support in the continuous-dual sense, not the support of a real-valued measure.

proofSteps: Both forward coordinates and the inverse are R-linear by restriction and native pushforward.

hypotheses: X is a compact topological space, s is a clopen subset, and R is a normed commutative ring. No field, completeness, ultrametricity, Hausdorffness of X, or nonemptiness of s is assumed. C(s,R) uses the subspace topology and its supremum norm; s is compact because it is closed in X. D(X,R) and D(s,R) are the existing AbstractMeasure carriers. No topology is installed on either measure carrier.
Y is compact and q∈C(X,Y); t is clopen in Y, and s is exactly its inverse image.

nodes.title: Unit-group measures as the kernel of psi
nodes.statement: Define AbstractMeasure.unitsMeasureEquivKerPsi p R : D(U,R) ≃ₗ[R] ker(psiMeasure p R), with forward value j_Uν and inverse r_U on the ambient value of a kernel element.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; Z=ℤ_p has its pinned topology and U=Zˣ is the existing units type with its existing topology. R is a normed commutative ring. E=unitRestriction p R and ψ=psiMeasure p R are the earlier ambient operators. Measures retain the existing AbstractMeasure carriers.
proofSteps: For ν, intrinsic-unit-restriction-section and intrinsic-unit-extension-projector give E(j_Uν)=j_Uν. The earlier unit-support-psi theorem gives ψ(j_Uν)=0, so native pushforward lands in the existing LinearMap.ker.
For μ in that kernel, unit-support-psi gives Eμ=μ. The projector comparison then gives j_U(r_Uμ)=μ. The other inverse identity is intrinsic-unit-restriction-section; both maps are R-linear.

The convolution non-example uses the native prodMk and map evaluation formulas: at p=2, additive convolution of δ₁ with itself pushes the pair (1,1) to δ₂, while multiplicative unit convolution gives δ₁. Their ambient measures differ by evaluation on x.

proofSteps: Use the earlier unit-measure-kernel-equivalence at integral coefficients. The pinned amiceTransformEquiv is an actual linear equivalence between D(Z,Z) and Z[[T]].

The existing planned psi-series-intertwining identity gives ψSeries(Aμ)=A(ψμ). Injectivity of A therefore identifies the two kernel conditions. Restrict A and A⁻¹ to those existing kernel submodules and compose with the unit-measure equivalence.
The value and inverse formulas follow from unit-measure-kernel-evaluation and unit-measure-kernel-inverse. Their inverse identities follow from those of the two linear equivalences.

The Dirac tests use native coeff_amiceTransform, dirac_apply and mahler_apply. For positive natural atoms use amice-dirac-natural. The first coefficient at −1 is −1 by Ring.choose_one_right, and the zeroth coefficient is total mass by Ring.choose_zero_right.

proofSteps: Use the native toCLMEquiv to identify the field-valued dual model with the existing measure carrier. The bounded coefficient and bounded inverse maps are linear.

nodes.title: Rational measures admit an integral power scaling
nodes.statement: For every ν∈D(Z_p,Q_p) there are n≥0 and μ∈D(Z_p,Z_p) such that ν=p^(−n)·extendIntegralCoefficients(μ).
hypotheses: p is prime; the coefficient field is the existing Q_p, with its canonical Z_p-algebra structure and bounded scalar action. The domain is Z_p. Integral measures are the existing AbstractMeasure(Z_p,Z_p,Z_p), and extension is the previously planned actual extendIntegralCoefficients map.
proofSteps: The native Q_p norm satisfies ‖p‖<1. Thus ‖p^n‖‖toCLMEquiv(ν)‖ tends to zero; choose n so this product is at most one. This also handles ν=0.
The native normed-space scalar norm identity puts p^nν in the unit ball. Apply rational-integral-image to obtain its unique integral antecedent μ.
Since p is nonzero in Q_p, multiply the equality by the inverse of p^n. This is existence of a common denominator for this measure, not a topology or localization equivalence.

nodes.statement: The existing map x ↦ delta_x from X to D(X,R) is continuous for the native weak topology.
hypotheses: X is any topological space; R is a normed commutative ring. Compactness, completeness and an ultrametric norm are not required. D(X,R) is the native continuous scalar-valued dual.
proofSteps: Unfold WeakTopology as the topology induced by evaluation into the product of copies of R indexed by continuous test functions.
For each test f, evaluation of delta_x is f(x). Apply continuous_induced_rng and continuous_pi to the continuity of f.
acceptance: The conclusion applies to integral coefficients, including R=Z_2; it is not a claim of operator-norm continuity.

nodes.statement: For each x in X, the native operator norm of delta_x is exactly 1.
hypotheses: X is compact; K is a nontrivially normed field. Norms are those of toCLMEquiv into the existing continuous K-linear dual. No ultrametric or completeness hypothesis is needed.
proofSteps: Pointwise evaluation is bounded by the supremum norm of f. The native opNorm_le_bound gives the upper bound 1.

nodes.title: Norm separation of distinct Dirac measures
nodes.statement: If x and y are distinct points of X, then the native operator norm of delta_x−delta_y is exactly 1.
hypotheses: X is compact and totally separated; K is a nontrivially normed field satisfying |a+b|≤max(|a|,|b|). No completeness is required.
proofSteps: The ultrametric inequality bounds |f(x)−f(y)| by the supremum norm of f, giving the operator upper bound 1.

Use exists_isClopen_of_totally_separated to choose a clopen U containing x and excluding y. Its native locally constant characteristic function has norm at most 1 and evaluates to 1 and 0 respectively. Applying le_opNorm to this test gives the lower bound 1.
acceptance: Over Q_2, delta_0−delta_1 has norm 1 even in the dyadic case. For x=y the norm is zero.
The ultrametric hypothesis matters: over the real field, the difference of the two point evaluations on a discrete two-point space has norm 2.

nodes.title: Failure of norm compactness of the measure unit ball
nodes.statement: The unit ball {L in the continuous K-linear dual of C(X,K) : norm(L)≤1} is not compact for its operator-norm topology.
hypotheses: X is infinite, compact and totally separated; K is a nontrivially normed ultrametric field. No properness or completeness of K is needed for this negative result.
proofSteps: Use Infinite.natEmbedding to choose distinct points of X. Their Dirac functionals lie in the unit ball by dirac-operator-norm, and every pair has distance 1 by dirac-difference-operator-norm.

If the unit ball were compact, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq would give a convergent subsequence. Its shift by one has the same limit, so the norms of the differences tend to zero. Strict monotonicity of the subsequence indices says every such norm is 1, contradicting uniqueness of limits in the real field.
acceptance: In particular the Q_p-valued measure unit ball on Z_p is not norm compact. Native WeakDual.isCompact_closedBall gives weak compactness over proper K; the two topologies must stay explicit.
The infinitude hypothesis cannot be removed: the Q_p dual unit ball on a one-point space is the compact ring Z_p.

nodes.statement: For every normed commutative ring R, the measures delta_(p^n) in D(Z_p,R) converge weakly to delta_0 as n tends to infinity.
hypotheses: p is prime, including 2. The domain points p^n lie in the native p-adic integer ring. The target measure topology is WeakTopology.
proofSteps: PadicInt.norm_p and p>1 give norm(p)<1, so tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_norm_lt_one gives p^n→0 in Z_p.
Compose that limit with dirac-weak-continuous. This is convergence against each fixed continuous test, not uniform convergence on the test unit ball.
acceptance: The same weak convergence holds both for integral Z_2 coefficients and for rational Q_2 coefficients.

nodes.statement: For every continuous f:X→Q_p there are n≥0 and a continuous g:X→Z_p such that g(x), viewed in Q_p, equals p^n f(x) for every x.
hypotheses: p is prime; X is compact. No group structure, total separation or nonemptiness of X is required.
proofSteps: The native supremum norm bounds every |f(x)|. Since norm(p)<1, the real quantities norm(p^n) norm(f) tend to zero; choose n for which this bound is at most 1.
Define g pointwise using the native subtype Z_p={z in Q_p : norm(z)≤1}. The pointwise norm bound supplies membership, and the continuous product p^n f has a continuous subtype lift.
acceptance: For f constantly 1/3 over Q_3, n=1 and g constantly 1 work; n=0 cannot work. For the zero test n=0 and g=0 work, including on the empty domain.

nodes.title: Weak continuity of integral coefficient extension
nodes.statement: The existing extendIntegralCoefficients map from D(Z_p,Z_p) to D(Z_p,Q_p) is continuous when both measure spaces carry their native weak topologies.
hypotheses: p is prime. Use the canonical Z_p-algebra structure on Q_p and its bounded scalar action, obtainable from the native subtype norm. The actual bounded-inverse coefficient extension is used.
proofSteps: For a fixed rational test f, rational-test-integral-scaling supplies a single n and integral test g with g=p^n f after coercion. The choice depends on f, not on the varying integral measure.

Coefficient-extension-test-function and Q_p-linearity give E(mu)(f)=p^(−n) times the coercion of mu(g). This is weakly continuous in mu because evaluation at g, the inclusion Z_p→Q_p, and multiplication by the fixed scalar are continuous.
Apply the induced-product criterion for the rational weak topology. Scaling every fixed test supplies continuity on the whole source; no common scaling exponent for all rational tests is claimed.
acceptance: This is continuity of the actual extension, not a map on formal series or a replacement measure carrier. The integral Dirac sequence therefore has the same rational weak limit.

nodes.statement: The native space D(Z_p,Z_p), equipped with WeakTopology, is compact.
hypotheses: p is prime. The topology is the weak topology of integral test evaluations; no norm is installed on this integral dual.
proofSteps: Use integral-amice-weak-homeomorphism to identify this space topologically with the native Z_p power series with coefficientwise p-adic topology.

That topology is the product topology on coefficients. Each Z_p is compact by PadicInt.compactSpace, so Pi.compactSpace applies. Pull compactness back along the existing Amice homeomorphism using the native closed-embedding compactness theorem.
acceptance: This compactness includes p=2. It concerns integral measures, not the entire rational weak dual; source finding E10 remains unchanged.

nodes.title: Weak topology on the integral unit ball
nodes.statement: The actual coefficient extension E:D(Z_p,Z_p)→D(Z_p,Q_p) is a closed embedding for the native weak topologies. Thus the integral weak topology agrees with the weak subspace topology on the rational unit ball identified by rational-integral-image.
hypotheses: p is prime. Use the canonical Z_p-algebra structure on Q_p and bounded scalar action. The unit ball means norm(toCLMEquiv(nu))≤1; its topology here is the weak subspace topology.
proofSteps: Integral-measures-weak-compact supplies compactness of the source, and integral-coefficient-extension-weak-continuous supplies continuity. Rational-integral-extension-injective supplies injectivity.
The rational weak topology is induced by the injective evaluation map into a product of Hausdorff copies of Q_p, hence is Hausdorff by IsEmbedding.t2Space. Apply Continuous.isClosedEmbedding.

The existing rational-integral-image node identifies the range with the rational operator unit ball. This is therefore a compact weak subspace, in agreement with native Banach–Alaoglu. The Dirac noncompactness theorem applies separately to its operator-norm topology.
acceptance: Over Q_2 the integral extension still gives this weak closed embedding. The image is weakly compact and norm closed, but is not norm compact.

The old inverse-Amice sequence for T^n remains weakly null; the primary exact norm comparison gives norm 1 for each rational extension. This recovers the source’s monomial example without identifying weak and uniform coefficient convergence.

hypotheses: p is any prime, including2; Z=Z_p and U=Z units with its native topology. Measures are the existing AbstractMeasure continuous duals. Apply the existing coefficient-extension-weight theorem. Its R-valued multiplier is the coefficient image of e, which equals the R-valued unit indicator pointwise because the algebra map preserves zero and one.
The same evaluation identity over R identifies the result with E_R(I_R μ). This uses the actual support projector, not a newly defined psi operator.

nodes.title: Integral unit measures form the rational unit ball
nodes.statement: For ν∈D(U,Q_p), there is a unique μ∈D(U,Z) with I_U,Q_p μ=ν if and only if the native operator norm of ν is at most one.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including2; Z=Z_p and U=Z units with its native topology. Measures are the existing AbstractMeasure continuous duals. For this rational comparison R=Q_p, with the canonical bounded Z_p-scalar action. Every displayed measure norm is the operator norm after the native toCLMEquiv. The integral carrier is not assigned the native field norm or an implicit topology.
proofSteps: If ν=I_U,Q_p μ, its norm is the bounded integral Amice coefficient norm, at most one by integral-coefficient-sequence and the norm of one in Q_p.
Conversely, include ν into D(Z,Q_p). Its norm is unchanged, so the ambient integral-image theorem supplies μ_0∈D(Z,Z) with I_Q_p μ_0=j_Q_p ν.
Set μ=r_Z μ_0. The restriction square gives I_U,Q_p μ=r_Q_p I_Q_p μ_0=r_Q_p j_Q_p ν=ν.
Uniqueness is the preceding rational-unit-extension-injective theorem. No compactness or false weak-to-norm continuity inference is used.
acceptance: The unit ball is closed and has radius one centered at zero in the native rational dual. A p^(-1)-scaled Dirac mass at the unit one lies outside it.

nodes.title: Local constancy of p-adic reduction
nodes.statement: The native ring homomorphism PadicInt.toZMod:Z_p→F_p is locally constant.
hypotheses: p is prime, including p=2. Z=Z_p is the native p-adic integer ring and k=ZMod p. B=Z[[T]] and B_0=k[[T]] are native PowerSeries carriers; Y=1+T. The integral psi is the existing Amice transport of the measure restriction/division operator.
proofSteps: At x, use the open ball of radius one. For y in this ball the native norm criterion says p divides y−x.

nodes.statement: For n≥0, psi(Y^n)=Y^(n/p) if p divides n in N, and psi(Y^n)=0 otherwise.
hypotheses: p is prime, including p=2. Z=Z_p is the native p-adic integer ring and k=ZMod p. B=Z[[T]] and B_0=k[[T]] are native PowerSeries carriers; Y=1+T. The integral psi is the existing Amice transport of the measure restriction/division operator.
proofSteps: The existing natural-Dirac Amice identity expresses Y^n as the transform of delta_n. Commute psi with this transform using psi-series-intertwining and apply psi-measure-dirac.
The kernel and maximal-ideal formulas for toZMod, together with natCast_eq_zero_iff, identify divisibility of n by p in Z_p with divisibility in N.
When p divides n, the equality n=p(n/p) and divide-by-p-mul show that the divided point is n/p. Transform the resulting Dirac mass back. When p does not divide n, the transformed measure is zero.
acceptance: The exponent is divided by p, not left equal to n; n=0 gives psi(1)=1.

nodes.title: Residue averaging operator
nodes.statement: Define the k-linear operator psi_0:B_0→B_0 to be the finite weighted sum of the existing Cartier power-series restrictions, psi_0(F)=sum_(0≤i<p) (−1)^i Lambda_i(F). Equivalently its nth coefficient is sum_(0≤i<p) (−1)^i coeff_(pn+i)(F).

proofSteps: Import the Cartier supplier only at positive modulus p and residues 0≤i<p. Its power-series restriction is the decimation coeff_n(Lambda_i F)=coeff_(pn+i)(F).

Take the finite weighted sum of these native linear maps. Alternatively construct the same map with PowerSeries.mk and the displayed coefficient formula; linearity is coefficientwise finite-sum algebra and coefficient extensionality identifies the two constructions.

The zero, sum and scalar APIs are linear-map laws. The coefficient characterization and weighted-Cartier characterization expose the construction; the separate monomial and left-inverse nodes provide the generator and Frobenius APIs.

The map is k-linear and is not multiplicative.

nodes.title: Pole-cancelled residue averaging identity
nodes.statement: For H in B_0, psi_0(Y T^(p−1) H(T^p))=Y H.
hypotheses: p is prime, including p=2. Z=Z_p is the native p-adic integer ring and k=ZMod p. B=Z[[T]] and B_0=k[[T]] are native PowerSeries carriers; Y=1+T. The integral psi is the existing Amice transport of the measure restriction/division operator.
proofSteps: Commute H(T^p) to the first factor and apply residue-psi-semilinear.

nodes.title: Vanishing of a shifted Frobenius fixed series
nodes.statement: If H in B_0 satisfies T^(p−1)H(T^p)=H, then H=0.
hypotheses: p is prime, including p=2. Z=Z_p is the native p-adic integer ring and k=ZMod p. B=Z[[T]] and B_0=k[[T]] are native PowerSeries carriers; Y=1+T. The integral psi is the existing Amice transport of the measure restriction/division operator.
proofSteps: Suppose H is nonzero and let d be its finite native power-series order. The order of T^(p−1) is p−1 and the native order_expand formula gives order(H(T^p))=pd.
The native order_mul theorem over the field F_p turns the assumed equality into d=p−1+pd.
Since p>1 and d≥0, the right side is strictly greater than d. This contradiction proves H=0.
acceptance: The prime hypothesis supplies p>1. At p=1 the analogous equation would hold for every H, so that case cannot be admitted.

nodes.statement: If psi_0(Y T^(p−1) H(T^p))=Y T^(p−1) H(T^p), then H=0; consequently the displayed error term is zero.
hypotheses: p is prime, including p=2. Z=Z_p is the native p-adic integer ring and k=ZMod p. B=Z[[T]] and B_0=k[[T]] are native PowerSeries carriers; Y=1+T. The integral psi is the existing Amice transport of the measure restriction/division operator.

nodes.statement: For a in Z and natural m,n, mahler_n(a m)=sum_(0≤k≤n) coeff_n(b_a^k) mahler_k(m).

Take coefficient n. Native coeff_subst gives a finite-support sum. Since b_a has constant coefficient zero, order(b_a^k)≥k; therefore coeff_n(b_a^k)=0 when k>n. The additive theorem generated by finprod_eq_prod_of_mulSupport_subset restricts the sum to k≤n.

acceptance: Allow a=0 and negative or nonintegral p-adic a. The bound on k is n, not a natural-number representative of a.

nodes.statement: For any metric space R, continuous functions U→R that factor through one of the red_n form a dense subset of C(U,R), with its native topology of uniform convergence.

hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2. R is a normed commutative ring with a ℤ_p-algebra structure and continuous ℤ_p-scalar action. Write j:ℤ_p→R for its algebra map, x_R for the continuous function t↦j(t), and M_(R,n) for t↦j(mahler_n(t)). Concretely these are the existing pointwise actions of the integral coordinate and Mahler functions on the constant-one R-valued test. No new function or measure carrier is introduced.

μ is a native R-valued AbstractMeasure on ℤ_p; Aμ is its existing native Amice transform. Write ∂_R for the already planned Mahler derivation (1+T)d/dT on R[[T]]. Completeness, ultrametricity, a field structure and characteristic zero are not needed for the weighting and ordinary-moment identities.
proofSteps: Evaluate the preceding integral mahler-recurrence at t∈ℤ_p and apply the existing algebra map j to both sides.

The ring homomorphism preserves products, sums and natural scalar multiples. The identity r•1=j(r), from Algebra.smul_def, identifies the resulting functions with x_R and M_(R,n). Continuous-function extensionality finishes.
This transports the integral recurrence rather than reconstructing the binomial functions in R. It uses no division by n+1 or n!, and does not assume that R itself has a binomial-ring structure.

nodes.title: The integral measure of finite unit coordinates
nodes.statement: Construct μ_c=ofUnitCoordinates(c):D(U,ℤ_p) as the unique continuous extension of I_c from locally constant tests.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2. U=ℤ_pˣ has its native compact topology; A_n=(ℤ/p^nℤ)ˣ for every n≥0. red_n is the existing actual unit reduction, and t_(m,n):A_n→A_m for m≤n is native ZMod.unitsMap. proofSteps: Use the existing native linear inclusion e=LocallyConstant.toContinuousMapLinearMap into C(U,ℤ_p). Its injectivity lets I_c descend uniquely to the native submodule range(e); use the inherited norm and topology on that range. This is a local proof construction, not another public function-space carrier.

The preceding norm bound becomes ‖I_c(x)‖≤‖x‖ on range(e). Native LinearMap.mkContinuous with bound one packages it as a continuous ℤ_p-linear functional. This native constructor works for rings, so ℤ_p is not treated as a field.

The range is dense: the existing dense finite unit tests are locally constant because red_n is continuous into a finite discrete space. The native subtype inclusion range(e).subtypeL is uniformly inducing by isUniformEmbedding_subtype_val.

Apply native ContinuousLinearMap.extend along this inclusion, using native completeness of ℤ_p. Its output is precisely the native continuous dual D(U,ℤ_p). Agreement follows from extend_eq. The semiring extension API supplies linearity; no field-only extendOfNorm theorem is used.

The zero, sum and scalar laws in the family variable follow from the finite pairing formula and equality of continuous maps on the dense locally constant range. Compatibility proofs for the zero, sum and scalar families are obtained by finite pushforward linearity; proof irrelevance removes their choices. At level zero the unique coefficient is the value on the constant-one test.
acceptance: This constructs an actual native measure. Identifying its input family with the owner’s completed group-algebra element and proving the topological algebra comparison remain separate targets.

nodes.statement: For every n, the sum of P_(n,a)μ over all a∈ZMod(p^n) equals μ.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2; n,m are natural numbers, including 0. Z=ℤ_p and ρ_n:Z→ZMod(p^n) is the native ring reduction. R is a normed commutative ring, possibly the zero ring. Measures are native D(Z,R).

nodes.title: Duals and biduals as intersections of localisations
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated torsion-free A-module, V = M ⊗_A K and V^∧ = Hom_K(V, K), and write M⁺ = Hom_A(M, A). Inside V^∧ and V: M⁺ = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} M⁺_𝔭 and M⁺⁺ = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} M_𝔭, and M is reflexive (the bidual map M → M⁺⁺ is an isomorphism) if and only if M = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} M_𝔭 (Lemma 5.1.2). For every finitely generated M the dual M⁺ is reflexive (Corollary 5.1.3), and reflexive modules are torsion-free (Definition 5.1.1, Remark).
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: (i): if λ ∈ ⋂ M⁺_𝔭 then λ(m) ∈ ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭 = A for every m ∈ M; the other inclusion is clear.
(ii): M_𝔭 is finitely generated torsion-free over the discrete valuation ring A_𝔭, hence free, so M_𝔭 → M_𝔭⁺⁺ is an isomorphism; identify V with V^∧∧ and apply (i) to M⁺.
(iii) follows from (ii); Corollary 5.1.3 applies (ii) to the finitely generated torsion-free module M⁺.
acceptance: Mathlib's Module.IsReflexive is the target notion; the intersection description is the new content.

nodes.title: Pseudo-null modules
nodes.statement: A finitely generated A-module M is pseudo-null if M_𝔭 = 0 for every prime 𝔭 of height at most one, equivalently if every prime containing ann_A(M) has height at least two (Definition 5.1.4). Pseudo-null modules are torsion; over a Dedekind domain only 0 is pseudo-null; over a two-dimensional noetherian integrally closed local domain with finite residue field a module is pseudo-null if and only if it is finite (Remarks 1–4). Submodules, quotients and extensions of pseudo-null modules are pseudo-null.
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: M_𝔭 = 0 if and only if some s ∉ 𝔭 kills M, i.e. ann_A(M) ⊄ 𝔭 (Remark 1).
Pseudo-null modules are torsion because M_(0) = M ⊗_A K = 0 (Remark 2).
Remark 4: a finite M has 𝔪^rM = 0, so supp(M) ⊆ {𝔪}; conversely supp(M) = V(ann M) ⊆ {𝔪} gives 𝔪^r ⊆ ann(M), and M is a finitely generated module over the finite ring A/𝔪^r.
Closure under submodules, quotients and extensions: localisation is exact (a worker addition; NSW uses it in Remark 2 after (5.1.7)).
acceptance: For A = O⟦T₁, …, T_d⟧ with d ≥ 2, pseudo-null does not mean finite: A/(T₁, T₂) is infinite with support of height two.

nodes.title: Pseudo-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: A homomorphism f : M → N of finitely generated A-modules is a pseudo-isomorphism, written M ≈ N, if ker f and coker f are pseudo-null, equivalently if f_𝔭 is an isomorphism for every prime 𝔭 of height at most one (Definition 5.1.5). For M torsion and α ≠ 0 with supp(A/αA) disjoint from supp(M) ∩ P(A), multiplication by α is a pseudo-isomorphism (Lemma 5.1.6). Between finitely generated torsion modules a pseudo-isomorphism M → N gives one N → M, so ≈ is an equivalence relation there (Remark 1 after 5.1.7). For general finitely generated modules it is not: over Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ the maximal ideal 𝔪 = ker(Λ → 𝔽_p) is torsion-free of rank one and not free, the inclusion 𝔪 → Λ is a pseudo-isomorphism, and there is no pseudo-isomorphism Λ → 𝔪 (§3, Exercise 1). Over O⟦T⟧ the pseudo-isomorphisms are the maps with finite kernel and cokernel, RJW §13.1's definition.
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: The two definitions agree because localisation is exact: f_𝔭 is an isomorphism iff (ker f)_𝔭 = (coker f)_𝔭 = 0.
Lemma 5.1.6: α is a unit in A_𝔭 for 𝔭 ∈ supp(M) ∩ P(A), and M_𝔭 = 0 at the remaining primes of height ≤ 1.

Symmetry for torsion modules: with S = A ∖ ⋃𝔭_i over the finitely many height-one primes in the supports, S⁻¹A is a semilocal principal ideal domain, f becomes an isomorphism over S⁻¹A, and clearing a denominator of its inverse gives g : N → M with g ∘ f and f ∘ g multiplication by some s ∈ S, pseudo-isomorphisms by Lemma 5.1.6.

Exercise 1 (not proved in the source): 𝔪 = (p, T) needs two generators (𝔪/𝔪² ≅ 𝔽_p²), so it is not free; a nonzero map Λ → 𝔪 is x ↦ xa with a ∈ 𝔪, and its cokernel 𝔪/aΛ has finite index in Λ/aΛ, which is infinite, having dimension one.
Agreement with RJW: over O⟦T⟧ pseudo-null means finite (pseudo-null, Remark 4).
acceptance: Pseudo-isomorphism is never declared an equivalence relation on arbitrary finitely generated modules.

nodes.title: Torsion modules over a normal domain up to pseudo-isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated A-module with torsion submodule T_A(M) and F_A(M) = M/T_A(M). (i) There is a pseudo-isomorphism M → T_A(M) ⊕ F_A(M). (ii) There are finitely many height-one primes 𝔭_i and integers n_i ≥ 1 with a pseudo-isomorphism T_A(M) → ⊕_i A/𝔭_i^{n_i}, and the families (𝔭_i), (n_i) are determined by T_A(M) up to renumbering (Proposition 5.1.7). An extension of finitely generated torsion modules whose height-one supports are disjoint is pseudo-isomorphic to their direct sum (Remark 2).
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: Let 𝔭₁, …, 𝔭_h be the height-one primes in supp(T_A(M)) and S = A ∖ ⋃𝔭_i. If h = 0, T_A(M) is pseudo-null and M → F_A(M), T_A(M) → 0 suffice.

S⁻¹A is a semilocal Dedekind domain, hence a principal ideal domain; S⁻¹T_A(M) is a direct summand of S⁻¹M, and Hom commutes with S⁻¹ for finitely generated M, so the projector is f₀/s₀ with f₀ : M → T_A(M); f₁ = s₁f₀ restricts to s₁s₀ on T_A(M).
(i): f = (f₁, can) : M → T_A(M) ⊕ F_A(M) has the same kernel and cokernel as f₁|T_A(M), a pseudo-isomorphism by Lemma 5.1.6.

(ii): choose an S⁻¹A-isomorphism S⁻¹T_A(M) ≅ S⁻¹E with E = ⊕ A/𝔭_i^{n_ij}, clear its denominator to g : T_A(M) → E, and apply Lemma 5.1.6; uniqueness from the structure theorem over the principal ideal domains A_𝔭.
acceptance: The statement needs only a noetherian integrally closed domain, so it covers the multivariable algebras O⟦T₁, …, T_d⟧ once their normality is supplied; that input is listed as remaining in the L4 coverage.

nodes.title: The reflexive hull is a pseudo-isomorphism
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated torsion-free A-module M, the bidual map φ_M : M → M⁺⁺ is an injective pseudo-isomorphism into a reflexive module (Proposition 5.1.8).
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
proofSteps: M_𝔭 is free over A_𝔭 for 𝔭 of height ≤ 1, so M_𝔭 → M_𝔭⁺⁺ is an isomorphism; M⁺⁺ is reflexive by Corollary 5.1.3; ker φ_M ⊗ K = 0, so ker φ_M is torsion inside a torsion-free module, hence zero.
acceptance: Free modules are their own reflexive hulls.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules over two-dimensional regular local rings are free
nodes.statement: Let A be an n-dimensional regular local ring, 2 ≤ n < ∞, with a regular system of parameters p₁, …, p_n generating the maximal ideal, and p₀ = 0. A finitely generated A-module M is free if and only if M/(p₀, …, p_i)M is a reflexive A/(p₀, …, p_i)-module for i = 0, …, n − 2. In particular every reflexive module over a two-dimensional regular local ring is free (Proposition 5.1.9, following Diekert).
hypotheses: A regular local of dimension n with 2 ≤ n < ∞, and integrally closed (automatic for regular local rings by Auslander–Buchsbaum, which is cited, not planned here).
proofSteps: M is reflexive, hence torsion-free, so p₁ acts injectively; take a minimal presentation φ : A^r → M.
If M/p₁M is free over A/p₁, Nakayama makes φ̄ : (A/p₁)^r → M/p₁M an isomorphism, so p₁ acts bijectively on ker φ and ker φ = 0 by Nakayama.
Freeness of M/p₁M reduces by induction to n = 2, using that A/p₁ is regular of dimension n − 1 with parameters p̄₂, …, p̄_n.
For n = 2, A/p₁ is a discrete valuation ring, M/p₁M = M⁺⁺/p₁ embeds in the torsion-free Hom_A(M⁺, A/p₁), so it is torsion-free, hence free.
acceptance: The regular-local-ring facts used (A/p₁ regular of dimension n − 1; a one-dimensional regular local ring is a discrete valuation ring) are standard inputs; for Λ = O⟦T⟧ they are explicit (A/ϖ = k⟦T⟧).

nodes.title: Structure theorem over a two-dimensional regular local ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a two-dimensional regular local ring and M a finitely generated A-module. There are finitely many height-one primes 𝔭_i, an integer r ≥ 0, integers n_i ≥ 1 and a pseudo-isomorphism M → A^r ⊕ ⊕_i A/𝔭_i^{n_i}. The data are determined by M: r = dim_K M ⊗_A K, {𝔭_i} = supp(M) ∩ P(A), and the n_i are unique (Theorem 5.1.10).
hypotheses: A two-dimensional regular local ring, integrally closed (see reflexive-free-over-regular-local).
proofSteps: Proposition 5.1.7(i) splits M up to pseudo-isomorphism as T_A(M) ⊕ F_A(M).
Proposition 5.1.8 embeds F_A(M) into its reflexive hull by an injective pseudo-isomorphism, and the hull is free by Proposition 5.1.9.
Proposition 5.1.7(ii) treats T_A(M); uniqueness from 5.1.7 and r = dim_K M ⊗ K.
acceptance: For A = Λ = O⟦T⟧ this is the input to the structure theorem for Iwasawa modules.

nodes.title: O⟦T⟧ is a two-dimensional regular local ring
nodes.statement: For O a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k, Λ = O⟦T⟧ is a noetherian, factorial, two-dimensional regular local ring with maximal ideal (ϖ, T), residue field k, complete for the (ϖ, T)-adic topology.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Noetherian: Mathlib's instance IsNoetherianRing R⟦X⟧ for noetherian R (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Ideal.lean).
Factorial: Mathlib's instance UniqueFactorizationMonoid R⟦X⟧ for a principal ideal domain R (same file).
Local with maximal ideal (ϖ, T): f is a unit iff its constant term is (PowerSeries.isUnit_iff_constantCoeff).
Dimension two: 0 ⊂ (T) ⊂ (ϖ, T) is a chain of primes, and dim R⟦X⟧ = dim R + 1 for noetherian R bounds it above; 𝔪 = (ϖ, T) is generated by dim Λ = 2 elements, so Λ is regular.
Completeness: the (ϖ, T)-adic topology is the product topology on coefficients, for which O⟦T⟧ is complete since O is.
acceptance: The dimension formula dim R⟦X⟧ = dim R + 1 is a cited commutative-algebra input.

nodes.title: The height-one primes of O⟦T⟧
nodes.statement: The height-one primes of Λ = O⟦T⟧ are (ϖ) and (F) for F an irreducible distinguished (Weierstraß) polynomial; a distinguished polynomial is irreducible in O⟦T⟧ if and only if it is irreducible in O[T] (Lemma 5.3.7, stated there for O = ℤ_p).
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Λ is factorial, so each height-one prime is (f) for an irreducible f.
If (f) ≠ (ϖ) then f ∉ (ϖ), so f mod 𝔪_O ≠ 0 and preparation writes (f) = (F) with F distinguished.

A factorisation of a distinguished F into non-units of O⟦T⟧ has factors of finite reduced degree whose distinguished parts multiply to F by uniqueness of preparation (PowerSeries.weierstrassDistinguished_mul, IsWeierstrassFactorization.unique); this replaces NSW's citation of Bourbaki AC VII §3.8.
acceptance: NSW proves the case O = ℤ_p; the argument uses only factoriality and preparation, so it holds verbatim with ϖ in place of p.

nodes.title: Mathlib's Weierstrass theory as NSW's division lemma and preparation theorem
nodes.statement: For f ∈ O⟦T⟧ of finite reduced degree s (the least n with a_n ∉ 𝔪_O), NSW's division lemma (5.3.1), Corollary 5.3.3 and preparation theorem (5.3.4) are Mathlib's Weierstrass division and factorisation at the maximal ideal: s is the order of f mod 𝔪_O (IsWeierstrassFactorization.natDegree_eq_toNat_order_map); a Weierstraß polynomial is Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt 𝔪_O; O[T]/(F) ≅ O⟦T⟧/(F) is IsWeierstrassFactorizationAt.algEquivQuotient; existence and uniqueness are exists_isWeierstrassFactorization and IsWeierstrassFactorization.unique. The one statement Mathlib lacks is the last clause of (5.3.4): the distinguished factor F is the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by T on the free O-module O⟦T⟧/(f) of rank s.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
NSW allows any complete noetherian local O with finite residue field; Mathlib needs IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal O) O.
proofSteps: A complete noetherian local ring is adically complete for its maximal ideal, which is the Mathlib hypothesis.
Reduced degree: IsWeierstrassFactorization.natDegree_eq_toNat_order_map identifies deg F with the order of f mod 𝔪_O.

Characteristic polynomial: O⟦T⟧/(f) = O⟦T⟧/(F) ≅ O[T]/(F) = AdjoinRoot F, a free O-module with power basis 1, T, …, T^{s−1} (AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' for monic F), on which T acts by the companion matrix of F; its characteristic polynomial is F (charpoly_leftMulMatrix).
acceptance: No second preparation theorem is planned; this node only matches hypotheses and adds the characteristic-polynomial clause.

sources.excerpt: Then there exists a unique decomposition f = F·u into a Weierstraß polynomial F of degree s and a unit u
sources.match: Division Lemma 5.3.1 (proof cited to Bourbaki AC VII §3.8), Definition 5.3.2, Corollary 5.3.3 and Theorem 5.3.4 with its proof. The known erratum for p. 290, l. 13 concerns this proof and is already reflected in version 2.3.

nodes.title: Nonzero power series: ϖ^μ · distinguished · unit, and finitely many zeros
nodes.statement: Every nonzero f ∈ O⟦T⟧ factors uniquely as f = ϖ^μ·F·u with μ ≥ 0, F a distinguished polynomial and u ∈ O⟦T⟧^×; μ is the least ϖ-adic valuation of a coefficient and deg F is the reduced degree of ϖ^{−μ}f. Consequently f has at most deg F zeros in the open unit disc of any complete valued field extending Frac O (for instance ℂ_p), and power series agreeing at infinitely many points of that disc are equal. The zero series is excluded: it vanishes everywhere.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: O⟦T⟧ is a domain. For f ≠ 0 the minimum μ of the coefficient valuations is attained, and ϖ^{−μ}f has a unit coefficient, i.e. finite reduced degree.
Preparation (weierstrass-adapter) factors ϖ^{−μ}f = F·u; uniqueness of μ and of preparation gives uniqueness.
For |x| < 1, u(x) lies in u(0) + (maximal ideal) with u(0) ∈ O^×, so u(x) ≠ 0; hence f(x) = 0 iff F(x) = 0, which has at most deg F roots.
If f, g agree at infinitely many points of the disc, f − g has infinitely many zeros, so f − g = 0.
acceptance: This is the adapter ColemanPowerSeries L1 requests, with the nonzero hypothesis its finding E10 asks for.

nodes.title: The polynomials ω_n and ξ_n
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0 put ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1, ω_{−1} = 1, and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1}. Then ω_n and ξ_n are distinguished polynomials over O (ω_n ≡ T^{p^n} and ξ_n ≡ T^{p^n − p^{n−1}} mod p for n ≥ 1), ω_n = ξ₀ξ₁⋯ξ_n with ξ₀ = T and ξ_k = Σ_{i<p}(1 + T)^{ip^{k−1}}, ω_n ∈ (𝔪_O, T)^{n+1}, and ⋂_n ω_nO⟦T⟧ = 0, so O⟦T⟧ = lim O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) (Definition 5.3.13 and the proof of Proposition 5.3.5). For a topological generator γ of Γ ≅ ℤ_p, O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) ≅ O[Γ/Γ_n] by T ↦ γ − 1; the resulting O⟦T⟧ ≅ O⟦Γ⟧ is requested from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9.
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: The binomial coefficients C(p^n, i), 0 < i < p^n, are divisible by p, so ω_n is monic with non-leading coefficients in pO; ξ_n = Σ_{i<p}(1 + T)^{ip^{n−1}} is monic of degree p^n − p^{n−1} with the same property, since ξ_n ≡ T^{p^n−p^{n−1}} mod p.
The factorisation telescopes; ω_{n+1} = ω_n·ξ_{n+1} with ξ_{n+1} ∈ (p, T) gives ω_n ∈ (p, T)^{n+1} by induction.
⋂(𝔪_O, T)^{n+1} = 0 (Krull intersection in the noetherian local ring Λ), and compactness makes O⟦T⟧ → lim O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) surjective.

nodes.title: Structure theorem for Iwasawa modules
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated module over Λ = O⟦T⟧. There are r ≥ 0, integers m_i ≥ 1, irreducible distinguished polynomials F_j and integers n_j ≥ 1, and a homomorphism M → E = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_i Λ/(ϖ^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_j Λ/(F_j^{n_j}) with finite kernel and cokernel. The number r, the multisets (m_i) and (n_j) and the ideals (F_j) are determined by M (Theorem 5.3.8 for O = ℤ_p). The μ-part is built from powers of the uniformizer ϖ, not of p: RJW Theorem 13.1 writes Λ/(p^{n_i}) over O_L⟦T⟧, which fails when L/ℚ_p is ramified (source finding E15).
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Apply structure-theorem-regular-dimension-two to Λ, which is a two-dimensional regular local ring (iwasawa-algebra-regular-local).
The height-one primes are (ϖ) and (F) (height-one-primes); both are principal, so 𝔭^n = (ϖ^n) or (F^n).
Over Λ pseudo-null means finite (pseudo-null, Remark 4), so the pseudo-isomorphism has finite kernel and cokernel.
Uniqueness: for principal 𝔭 = (π), (Λ/π^n)_𝔭 has length n, and the lengths at each height-one prime are pseudo-isomorphism invariants.
acceptance: For O ramified over ℤ_p with index e, Λ/(ϖ) is not pseudo-isomorphic to any Λ^r ⊕ ⊕Λ/(p^{n_i}) ⊕ ⊕Λ/(F_j^{m_j}): its length at (ϖ) is 1, while Λ/(p^n) = Λ/(ϖ^{en}) has length en there and Λ/(F^m) has length 0.

nodes.title: Iwasawa invariants and the characteristic polynomial
nodes.statement: For M as in the structure theorem: the Λ-rank r(M) = r, the μ-invariant μ(M) = Σ_i m_i (counted in powers of ϖ), the λ-invariant λ(M) = Σ_j n_j deg F_j, and the characteristic polynomial F_{M,γ} = ∏_j F_j^{n_j} (Definition 5.3.9 for O = ℤ_p). They depend only on the pseudo-isomorphism class of M; r, μ and λ do not depend on the generator γ, but F_{M,γ} does; F_M = F_{T_Λ(M)}; μ and λ are additive and F_M multiplicative in short exact sequences of finitely generated torsion modules; a finitely generated torsion module is finite if and only if μ = λ = 0; and λ(M) = dim_{Frac O} M ⊗_O Frac O, with F_M the characteristic polynomial of T on that space (Remarks 1–3).
hypotheses: O is a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ and finite residue field k of characteristic p, and Λ = O⟦T⟧. NSW specialises to O = ℤ_p from (5.3.6) on; over O the vertical factors are powers of ϖ, not of p.
proofSteps: Well-definedness from uniqueness in the structure theorem.
μ(M) is the length of M_{(ϖ)} over the discrete valuation ring Λ_{(ϖ)}, and λ(M) = dim M ⊗_O Frac O; both are additive because localisation and ⊗ Frac O are exact.
Remark 3: finite modules and Λ/(ϖ^m) vanish after ⊗ Frac O, and Λ/(F) ⊗ Frac O = Frac O[T]/(F), on which T has characteristic polynomial F (weierstrass-adapter).
Independence of γ: γ ↦ γ^a (a ∈ ℤ_p^×) is the automorphism T ↦ (1 + T)^a − 1, which fixes (ϖ) and maps a distinguished F to a series of the same reduced degree, whose distinguished part replaces F.
Finite iff μ = λ = 0: then the elementary module is 0 and M has finite kernel and cokernel to 0.
acceptance: μ is normalised by v_ϖ; the class-number normalisation is O = ℤ_p, where μ is Iwasawa's μ.

sources.excerpt: Furthermore, a ﬁnitely generated Λ-torsion module M is ﬁnite if and only if λ(M) = 0 = µ(M)

nodes.title: The characteristic ideal
nodes.statement: For A a noetherian integrally closed domain and M a finitely generated torsion A-module, the characteristic divisor is div_A(M) = Σ_{𝔭∈P(A)} length_{A_𝔭}(M_𝔭)·[𝔭], a finite sum; when A is factorial, char_A(M) = ∏_{𝔭∈P(A)} 𝔭^{length_{A_𝔭}(M_𝔭)} is a principal ideal. It is multiplicative in short exact sequences, invariant under pseudo-isomorphism, equal to (f) on A/(f) for f ≠ 0, and equal to A exactly when M is pseudo-null. For Λ = O⟦T⟧, char_Λ(M) = (ϖ^{μ(M)}·F_{M,γ}), which is RJW Definition 13.3 with p^n read as ϖ^n (E15). It transforms under ring automorphisms of Λ (twisting by a character, inversion γ ↦ γ^{−1}, change of generator) by the inverse automorphism; under finite flat O → O′ it extends to Λ′ = O′⟦T⟧; and for O finite over ℤ_p, restricting scalars to ℤ_p⟦T⟧ takes the norm. A finite module has char = A while its initial Fitting ideal can be proper: Fitt₀(Λ/(p, T)) = (p, T).
hypotheses: A is a commutative noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K; P(A) is its set of height-one primes, at which A_𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, and A = ⋂_{𝔭∈P(A)} A_𝔭.
Λ, O as in the structure theorem for the comparison.
proofSteps: Finiteness: supp(M) ∩ P(A) consists of the finitely many minimal primes over ann(M) ≠ 0 of height one.
Multiplicativity (RJW Lemma 13.6, cited there to Coates–Sujatha): localisation is exact and length is additive (Module.length_eq_add_of_exact).
Pseudo-isomorphism invariance: f_𝔭 is an isomorphism for every height-one 𝔭; pseudo-null ⇔ all lengths vanish.
Cyclic value: (A/f)_𝔭 = A_𝔭/f has length v_𝔭(f) over the discrete valuation ring A_𝔭, and ∏𝔭^{v_𝔭(f)} = (f) in a factorial domain.
Comparison on Λ: evaluate on the elementary module, where (Λ/ϖ^m)_{(ϖ)} has length m and (Λ/F^n)_{(F)} length n.

Functoriality: an automorphism σ of A permutes height-one primes and preserves lengths, giving char(σ^*M) = σ^{−1}(char M); for finite flat O → O′, localisation at the primes of Λ′ over 𝔭 multiplies lengths by the ramification of 𝔭Λ′, i.e. char_{Λ′}(Λ′ ⊗ M) = char_Λ(M)Λ′.

Restriction of scalars (the norm formula requested by NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa, cited there to Bourbaki AC VII §4.8): reduce by multiplicativity and pseudo-isomorphism to Λ_O/(f), which as a ℤ_p⟦T⟧-module is the cokernel of the injective endomorphism f of Λ_O ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧^{[O:ℤ_p]}; localising at height-one primes, its characteristic ideal is (det f) = (N(f)).
Fitting: Λ/(p, T) has the presentation Λ² → Λ with image (p, T), so Fitt₀ = (p, T) ≠ Λ.
acceptance: The intrinsic length definition, the functoriality and the norm formula are worker derivations: NSW define only F_{M,γ} and RJW define Ch_Λ through the structure theorem.
Fitting ideals are requested from the Tau Ceti StableReduction roadmap, Layer 1.

nodes.title: Isotypic decomposition over Λ(H × ℤ_p) with #H prime to p
nodes.statement: Let Γ = H × Γ′ with H finite abelian of order prime to p and Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p, so Λ(Γ) ≅ O[H] ⊗ Λ, and let O contain the values of the characters of H. The idempotents e_ω = (1/#H)Σ_{a∈H} ω^{−1}(a)[a] ∈ O[H] are orthogonal with Σ_ω e_ω = 1, Λ(Γ) ≅ ⊕_ω Λ, and every Λ(Γ)-module decomposes as M = ⊕_ω M^{(ω)} with M^{(ω)} = e_ωM, on which H acts through ω; M is finitely generated torsion over Λ(Γ) if and only if each M^{(ω)} is over Λ (RJW Lemma 13.4). The characteristic ideal is char_{Λ(Γ)}(M) = ⊕_ω char_Λ(M^{(ω)}) (Definition 13.5), multiplicative in exact sequences (Lemma 13.6). Without enlarging O, the Galois-orbit idempotents e_{[ω]} ∈ O[H] give O[H] ≅ ⊕_{[ω]} O(ω).
hypotheses: H finite abelian, p ∤ #H, so #H ∈ O^×; O contains the character values, or orbits are used.
proofSteps: Orthogonality of characters gives e_ωe_ω′ = δ_{ωω′}e_ω and Σe_ω = 1; ae_ω = ω(a)e_ω for a ∈ H.
Each Λ(Γ)e_ω ≅ Λ, since H acts through the scalar ω.
Finite generation and torsion pass to and from the finitely many summands.
Definition 13.5 and multiplicativity then follow componentwise from characteristic-ideal.
acceptance: When p divides #H there is no such decomposition; the group ring is kept and nothing divides by #H.

nodes.title: Invariants, the discrete part M_δ and the cyclotomic part M_cycl
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated Λ-module. For a short exact sequence 0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0 there is an exact sequence 0 → M₁^Γ → M₂^Γ → M₃^Γ → (M₁)_Γ → (M₂)_Γ → (M₃)_Γ → 0 (Lemma 5.3.11). M_δ = ⋃_n M^{Γ_n} is Λ-torsion and finitely generated over ℤ_p, so d(M) < ∞; M₀ = tor_{ℤ_p}M_δ is the maximal finite Λ-submodule; supp(M_δ) ∩ P(Λ) ⊆ {(ξ_n)} and M_δ ≈ ⊕Λ/ξ_{n_i} with n_i ≤ d(M); (M/M_δ)_δ is ℤ_p-torsion-free; for torsion M, M^{Γ_n} is finite for all n iff d(M) = −1 (Lemma 5.3.14). The iterated M_cycl ⊇ M_δ is Λ-torsion, finitely generated over ℤ_p, pseudo-isomorphic to ⊕_k Λ/(ξ_{n_k})^{t_k}, and supp(M/M_cycl) ∩ P(Λ) avoids every (ξ_n) (Lemma 5.3.16).
hypotheses: Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p with a chosen topological generator γ, T = γ − 1; Γ_n is the subgroup of index p^n, ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1} (ω_{−1} = 1).
d(M) is the least d with Γ_d acting trivially on M_δ/M₀, and −1 if that quotient is 0 (Definition 5.3.12).
proofSteps: Lemma 5.3.11: the snake lemma on 0 → M_i^Γ → M_i → M_i → (M_i)_Γ → 0, multiplication by γ − 1.

Lemma 5.3.14: M_δ is finitely generated because Λ is noetherian, so some Γ_n acts trivially on it; ω_{d(M)} kills M_δ/M₀; (iv) from the limit of the coinvariant sequences, whose transition maps are multiplication by p^{m−n} for large n.
Lemma 5.3.16: from the structure theorem, M_i ≈ ⊕_k Λ/(ξ_{n_k})^{min(t_k, i)} and the chain M₀ ⊆ M₁ ⊆ ⋯ stabilises.

nodes.title: Iwasawa's growth formula
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated torsion Λ-module and n₀ ≥ d(M). Then #(M/(ω_n/ω_{n₀})M) = p^{μp^n + λn + ν} for all sufficiently large n, where μ = μ(M), λ = λ(M) and ν does not depend on n (Proposition 5.3.17). The key lemma: if M is free of rank λ over ℤ_p, then (ω_{n+1}/ω_n)M = pM for n > λ(λ − 1)/2 (Lemma 5.3.18). When d(M) = −1, taking n₀ = −1 (ω_{−1} = 1) gives #M_{Γ_n} = #M/ω_nM = p^{μp^n+λn+ν}.
hypotheses: Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p with a chosen topological generator γ, T = γ − 1; Γ_n is the subgroup of index p^n, ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1} (ω_{−1} = 1).
proofSteps: ν_n = ω_n/ω_{n₀} is prime to supp(M) ∩ P(Λ) for n ≥ n₀, so multiplication by ν_n is a pseudo-isomorphism (Lemma 5.1.6) and M/ν_nM is finite.
ν_n is injective on M/M₀, so #M/ν_n = #(M/M₀)/ν_n · #M₀/ν_n, and the second factor is eventually constant.
For N = M/M₀ ⊆ E (elementary, finite cokernel C), #N/ν_n = #E/ν_n by the snake lemma.
#(Λ/p^m)/ν_n = p^{m(p^n − p^{n₀})}; for E_j = Λ/F_j^{n_j}, Lemma 5.3.18 gives #E_j/ν_{n+1} = p^{n_j deg F_j}·#E_j/ν_n for n ≫ 0.

Lemma 5.3.18: T is nilpotent on M/pM, so γ lies in a p-Sylow subgroup of GL(λ, 𝔽_p) and γ^{p^m} = 1 on M/pM for m ≥ λ(λ − 1)/2; for n > λ(λ − 1)/2, A^{p^n} ≡ I mod p², so Σ_{k<p}A^{p^nk} = pU with U invertible.
acceptance: Stated for O = ℤ_p, the class-number normalisation the stage asks for.
Lemma 5.3.18 is checked for λ = 1, p = 3 in the suggested file.

nodes.title: No finite submodules, freeness and the minimal resolution
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated Λ-module M: (i) pd_Λ M ≤ 1 ⇔ M^{Γ_n} is ℤ_p-free for some (equivalently every) n ⇔ M has no nontrivial finite Λ-submodule; (ii) M is free if and only if M^Γ = 0 and M_Γ is ℤ_p-free (Proposition 5.3.19). With d₀ = dim_{𝔽_p} H⁰(Γ, M)/p, d₁ = dim_{𝔽_p} ₚH⁰(Γ, M) + dim_{𝔽_p} H¹(Γ, M)/p and d₂ = dim_{𝔽_p} ₚH¹(Γ, M), there is an exact sequence 0 → Λ^{d₂} → Λ^{d₁} → Λ^{d₀} → M → 0, and rank_Λ M = d₀ − d₁ + d₂ = rank_{ℤ_p} M_Γ − rank_{ℤ_p} M^Γ (Proposition 5.3.20).
hypotheses: Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p with a chosen topological generator γ, T = γ − 1; Γ_n is the subgroup of index p^n, ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1} (ω_{−1} = 1).
proofSteps: (ii): for a minimal presentation 0 → K → Λ^d → M → 0, Lemma 5.3.11 gives 0 = M^Γ → K_Γ → ℤ_p^d → M_Γ → 0; minimality and freeness of M_Γ make the right map an isomorphism, so K_Γ = 0 and K = 0 by Nakayama.
(i): a length-one free resolution embeds M^{Γ_n} in a free module; M₀ = 0 iff M₀^{Γ_n} = 0; conversely apply (ii) to the kernel of a presentation.

nodes.title: Finite coinvariants and the Euler characteristic formula
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated torsion Λ-module M and n ≥ 0 the following are equivalent: (i) M_{Γ_n} is finite; (ii) M^{Γ_n} is finite; (iii) F_{M,γ}(ζ − 1) ≠ 0 for every ζ with ζ^{p^n} = 1, a condition independent of γ. When they hold, #M^{Γ_n}/#M_{Γ_n} = p^{−μ(M)p^n}·∏_{ζ^{p^n}=1}|F_{M,γ}(ζ − 1)|_p (§3, Exercise 3).
hypotheses: Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ for Γ ≅ ℤ_p with a chosen topological generator γ, T = γ − 1; Γ_n is the subgroup of index p^n, ω_n = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 and ξ_n = ω_n/ω_{n−1} (ω_{−1} = 1).
proofSteps: The source states this as an exercise; this proof is a worker derivation.

χ_n(M) = #M^{Γ_n}/#M_{Γ_n} is multiplicative in short exact sequences of torsion modules with finite terms, by the six-term sequence of Lemma 5.3.11 for Γ_n, and χ_n = 1 on finite modules (0 → M^{Γ_n} → M → M → M_{Γ_n} → 0).

So reduce along the pseudo-isomorphism to the elementary module: Λ/(p^m) has no Γ_n-invariants and coinvariants (ℤ/p^m)[Γ/Γ_n] of order p^{mp^n}; Λ/(F) with F prime to ω_n has no invariants and #Λ/(F, ω_n) = |Res(F, ω_n)|_p^{−1} = ∏_ζ|F(ζ − 1)|_p^{−1}.
Finiteness: M_{Γ_n} is finite iff ω_n is prime to every F_j, i.e. F_j(ζ − 1) ≠ 0, and the same for invariants.
acceptance: Checked on M = Λ/(T − p), n = 0: #M_Γ = p, M^Γ = 0, and |F(0)|_p = |−p|_p = 1/p (suggested file).
